items.title: API revocation does not protect every authenticated SSR page
items.verification: Parent source-verified; no HTTP exploit attempted
items.problem: Some protected pages verify the JWT and its old grants but not live user status/tokenVersion. An old unexpired cookie can still reach page data after API access is revoked.
items.fix: Use one live-session resolver before both API and protected Server Component reads; preserve separate token-bound public-share access.
items.regression: Deactivate/delete/downgrade/reset a user; old cookie must return no protected data through API or SSR routes.

items.title: Report share listing exposes organization-wide bearer links to personal-scope viewers
items.verification: Parent source-verified; no live token requested
items.problem: Creation requires canSeeEveryone, but GET listing only checks report-module visibility. A personal-scope viewer can obtain an existing all-organization share token.
items.fix: Apply organization-wide scope authorization to listing tokens, not only creation. Review revoke/list ownership consistently.
items.regression: Create inward/leave shares as a manager; ordinary scoped users must not receive tokens.

checks.parent_source_review: Everyone scope checked before fetching tokens; module filtering and separate revocation permissions preserved.

items.title: FMS submitted fields can override server reference data
items.verification: Parent source-verified; requires reference-bound action template
items.problem: Arbitrary client form keys overwrite trusted reference values in resolvedFields, including SKU/quantity when a ledger action binds to those fields.
items.fix: Validate declared editable form fields, distinguish trusted reference bindings from user fields, and reject undeclared/reference-only keys.
items.regression: Assigned user submits forged reference SKU/quantity; action must reject and write no ledger movement.

items.title: WhatsApp destination filtering misses private IPv6 and resolved destinations
items.verification: Parent network-free probe confirmed IPv6 filter bypass; internal reachability unverified
items.problem: The actual filter accepted HTTPS IPv4-mapped loopback and IPv6 link-local addresses. Hostname-only screening does not establish safe DNS/redirect destinations.
items.fix: Prefer an approved provider-host policy; if custom hosts are needed, validate IPv4/IPv6 resolved connections and redirects with an egress-safe transport.
items.regression: Reject mapped loopback, link-local, private DNS answers and unsafe redirects; use mock transport, never probe production internals.

items.title: Suspended/expired tenants can request Blob upload authorization
items.verification: Parent source-verified; no token requested
items.problem: Upload only checks live user session, not live tenant status/trial; quota enforcement is absent in inspected route.
items.fix: Resolve allowed tenant before token generation; introduce explicit upload authorization/usage policy without changing provider plans.
items.regression: Valid user in suspended/expired tenant must receive no upload token; active tenant workflow must still work.

items.title: Credit/debit-note spending is not serialized and commits separately from accounting
items.verification: Parent CN source-verified; DN specialist-verified; concurrency not reproduced
items.problem: A guarded INSERT checks aggregate usage without serializing on a common note balance. Overlapping default-isolation statements can both admit spending. Usage then commits before its payment/journal batch. Earlier documentation calling the race closed is insufficient.
items.fix: Serialize note spending inside one complete transaction/routine; lock parent before a subsequent balance read or atomically debit a maintained balance. Commit usage/payment/journal together; add durable operation identity.
items.regression: Barrier-synchronize 60+60 against 100 across apply/refund/receive; inject journal failure; assert no overspend/orphan usage and safe retry.

items.title: Dispatch confirmation can duplicate effects or lose consumption increments
items.verification: Parent source-verified; concurrency not executed
items.problem: Shipment claim and stock sufficiency are pre-reads. No unique shipment-to-dispatch key is shown; numbering retries do not revalidate shipment. Consumed quantity is written as an absolute total from a stale snapshot.
items.fix: Add tenant/shipment uniqueness, atomic claim and stock validation; increment consumed quantity under guards and serialize related SKU writes. Keep all effects atomic and idempotent.
items.regression: Confirm the same shipment concurrently and separate shipments sharing a line; require one dispatch per shipment and exact stock/consumption totals.

items.title: Stock availability policy diverges and authoritative reads fail open
items.verification: Parent source-verified; competing writes not executed
items.problem: Order reservations subtract consumed quantity correctly, but failures become empty reservation maps. FMS Out and some PPC checks omit order reservations. Multiple writers can also validate the same free stock.
items.fix: Centralize write-side availability including all commitments, add back only the caller reservation, fail closed on authoritative-read failure, and serialize tenant/SKU mutations.
items.regression: Reserve for Orders then attempt FMS/PPC/manual consumption; inject reservation query failure; synchronize competing claims.

items.title: FMS/PPC/receipt/PO lifecycle commands can partially commit and replay
items.verification: Parent FMS source-verified; other paths specialist-reviewed; failure scenarios not injected
items.problem: Stock actions precede final workflow state; plan materials and receipts are updated separately; PO header/lines/indent linkage are separate writes. Failure or retry can duplicate stock or strand workflow state.
items.fix: Build narrow atomic domain commands, guarded state transitions and operation-level idempotency. Enforce indent ownership; emit external effects only after commit.
items.regression: Fault-inject at every boundary and retry; concurrently complete/start/receive/issue; assert exactly-once movements and consistent successors.

items.title: Business success and GL success are not durably coupled
items.verification: Parent source-verified; outage/race scenarios not executed
items.problem: Invoice issuance and payments can succeed while GL posting only logs failure. Concurrent issue can double-post. Payment journal source is order ID rather than unique payment ID.
items.fix: Atomic document/payment plus journal where feasible; otherwise durable transactional outbox with immutable per-event IDs, idempotent consumers and reconciliation.
items.regression: Concurrent issue, edit-versus-issue, repeated recovery and two genuine payments; require one journal per real event, no missing or duplicated accounting.

items.title: SKU identity is platform-wide rather than tenant-local
items.verification: Parent source-verified; already documented
items.problem: items.sku is the sole primary key; two organizations cannot use the same SKU. Other business references often have organization FKs but no composite tenant-owned relationship constraints.
items.fix: Plan a reviewed migration to (org_id, sku) identity and compatible tenant-scoped FKs/checks. Inspect all usage and data before altering keys.
items.regression: Same SKU in different tenants succeeds; cross-tenant/missing business references and invalid quantities are rejected.

items.title: Additional balance/allocation gates remain read-then-write
items.verification: Specialist source-reviewed; some gaps already documented; no runtime reproduction
items.problem: Split-invoice remaining value, petty-cash spending and shipment allocations need contention-safe admission, not only a sequential check. Dispatch invoice lookup also needs explicit any-Issued semantics for split invoices.
items.fix: Use serialized guarded balance/allocation transitions; make dispatch invoice gating a tenant/order/status-filtered EXISTS.
items.regression: Competing invoices/cash expenses/shipments cannot jointly exceed caps; test Draft+Issued invoices in both insertion orders.

items.title: Leave activation and recurring-work creation do not compose safely
items.verification: Parent reassignment/cron source-verified; interleavings not executed
items.problem: Reassignment precedes audit. Already activated leave is skipped, so newly generated work can stay with absent original doer. Read-before-insert recurring dedupe lacks a durable cycle identity.
items.fix: Atomically reassign with audit, resolve active leave ownership at task/FMS creation, and constrain recurring natural-cycle identity.
items.regression: Create work during active leave; inject audit failure; run cron concurrently; revert without disturbing completed buddy work.

items.title: Zero-pay deductions can produce negative net payroll
items.verification: Parent executed actual pure calculation; no DB/live payroll used
items.problem: With monthlySalary 20000, grossPay 0 and PF enabled, actual function returns employee PF 1800, yielding net -1800 in the caller calculation. PF/TDS calculation code exists despite stale notes. Generate/finalize also lack one serialized write boundary.
items.fix: Define explicit earned-pay/deduction policy and validate zero/partial-pay cases; snapshot calculation inputs/version; serialize generation/finalization. Obtain domain review rather than blindly clamping totals.
items.regression: Zero employed days, partial month, deduction flags and generate/finalize contention; finalized slips must remain immutable. No statutory-compliance conclusion is asserted.

items.title: Plan/user admission is inconsistent across create/reactivate/background paths
items.verification: Parent reactivation source-verified; background findings specialist-reviewed
items.problem: Active-user cap is checked on creation but not reactivation. Explicit cron tenant context can bypass trial-expiry resolution; whether generation should continue is a business-policy decision.
items.fix: Enforce cap on every admission under an org-level serialized check; define expired-trial maintenance versus business-generation policy explicitly.
items.regression: Reactivate at cap; two concurrent final-slot admissions; expired-trial interactive/background policy matrix.

items.title: Repeated tenant and settings reads persist outside repaired chatbot turn
items.verification: Source-reviewed; no new latency benchmark
items.problem: Multiple helpers independently resolve tenant or load all settings. Parallel per-key calls still multiply query volume. The local chatbot fix already removes this on its message route.
items.fix: Extend validated request-scoped tenant reuse and one settings snapshot per operation. Avoid global cross-request authorization caches; use correct server-component request scoping.
items.regression: Instrument query counts by endpoint and verify immediate revocation/concurrent-tenant isolation; measure before/after instead of promising milliseconds.

items.title: Inventory repeatedly scans lifetime ledger and full snapshot for one SKU
items.verification: Parent source-verified; scaling impact inferred
items.problem: Per-item ADC calculations scan full ledger; one-SKU detail builds the whole snapshot. Work grows with item count times history size.
items.fix: Precompute ADC by SKU in one pass; push SKU/date/open-indent filters and aggregates into SQL; paginate movement history.
items.regression: Scale item count/history independently and compare rows, CPU and timings while preserving reservation/ADC rounding semantics.

items.title: Aging has per-order reads; balance sheet repeats trial-balance work
items.verification: Specialist source-reviewed; no measurements
items.problem: Aging sequentially fetches payment/order information; credit risk inherits this. Balance sheet derives P&L through a second trial-balance read.
items.fix: Batch minimal payment/order projections; reuse the same trial-balance snapshot; consider SQL aggregates after equivalence tests.
items.regression: Assert bounded query growth and identical aging buckets, split invoices, retained earnings and IST date boundaries.

items.title: Global search and reports load full collections for small results
items.verification: Specialist source-reviewed; performance inferred
items.problem: Search filters full allowed-module lists, sometimes with unused details; report date/ownership filtering often occurs after full reads; tables lack bounded pages.
items.fix: Thin tenant-scoped SQL search projections/limits, filter pushdown, pagination and stale-response handling. Do not assume substring search gets indexed automatically.
items.regression: Increasing historical data should not proportionally inflate search transfer; verify grants, query result limits and report-equivalence.

items.title: Chat prompt limit does not limit transcript database reads
items.verification: Parent source-verified
items.problem: recentSessionMessages loads all transcript rows then slices to 20. Database transfer grows for long conversations despite bounded Gemini prompt.
items.fix: SQL descending stable ordering with LIMIT then reverse; paginate transcript and session UI independently.
items.regression: Long transcript returns only bounded recent rows in correct order with tie handling and unchanged tenant/ownership checks.

items.title: External request deadlines and recipient concurrency are incomplete
items.verification: Specialist source-reviewed; no provider load or outage simulation
items.problem: Serial sends plus repeated sender settings scale tenant duration. Individual provider fetches have no explicit application deadline. Bounded retry count does not bound a hanging call.
items.fix: Load sender config once, use bounded recipient workers and per-call/overall abort budgets. Preserve selective Gemini retries; avoid unsafe duplicate WhatsApp retries.
items.regression: Mock hanging response headers/body, overload and failure; verify concurrency ceiling, deadline, accounting and duplicate protection.

items.title: Board fetches can show stale tabs or errors as empty data
items.verification: Parent Orders source-verified; browser scenario not executed
items.problem: Uncancelled requests share state and ignore response status. Late old-tab results can replace newer results; JSON 403/500 can become empty arrays.
items.fix: Check res.ok; cancel and identify requests; set pending state at action; retain last good data with explicit retry; preserve drafts on transport errors.
items.regression: Resolve A after B; JSON 403/500 and offline mutations must show correct data/errors without losing input.

items.title: Chat replies/history are not isolated to originating conversation
items.verification: Parent source-verified; browser race not reproduced
items.problem: Session switching remains possible during loading/sending. Late responses modify current transcript; rollback slice(0,-1) can remove another conversation message.
items.fix: Track state/pending responses per session and optimistic ID; ignore stale responses or deliberately block switching during send.
items.regression: Delay A send/history, switch to B/New Chat, resolve or reject A; B must remain unchanged.

items.title: Hand-built modal drawer lacks modal focus behavior
items.verification: Parent drawer source-verified; keyboard/browser not freshly tested
items.problem: aria-modal drawer lacks focus trap, initial/return focus and background inertness; independent Escape listeners can affect multiple overlays.
items.fix: Use existing dialog primitive with drawer positioning; explicit scoped focus/Escape behavior for nonmodal chat.
items.regression: Tab/Shift+Tab stay in drawer, Escape closes intended overlay, focus returns correctly; nested overlays are independent.

items.title: Collapsed sidebar group toggles do not reveal destinations
items.verification: Parent source-verified
items.problem: Click toggles group but children only render when not collapsed; ARIA may claim expansion without visible panel.
items.fix: Wire group activation to shell expansion or an accessible rail popover; synchronize visible panel and ARIA state.
items.regression: Each collapsed group works by mouse and keyboard without separately finding the rail expand control.

items.title: Several visible form labels lack programmatic control association
items.verification: Specialist source-reviewed; accessibility tree not captured
items.problem: Sibling labels without htmlFor/id or ARIA naming do not name controls, especially repeated quantity/rate fields.
items.fix: Stable IDs, associated labels with line/item context, aria-describedby and aria-invalid for validation.
items.regression: Inspect accessible names, label click focus and per-line error announcement.

items.title: Financial/stock contention and recovery regressions are too sparse
items.verification: Collected suite/results verified earlier this same session; coverage source-reviewed
items.problem: Passing tooling does not prove concurrency correctness. Money/stock paths lack broad automated contention/fault/replay tests; manual live scripts do not run through CI Vitest include. One existing credit-overdue test fails on original code too.
items.fix: Prioritize domain/API invariant tests and a small browser business journey. Diagnose old test with deterministic backdating/persisted-term assertions, not changed expectations.
items.regression: Concurrent CN/DN/invoice/dispatch/receipt, injected failure, replay and foreign-tenant IDs; assert balances/stock/GL invariant and no foreign writes.

items.title: Disposable organization is not proof of isolated test database or cleanup
items.verification: Parent CI/setup source-verified; fixture risks specialist-reviewed; actual DB secret target unknown
items.problem: Generic DATABASE_URL has no test-only target guard; cleanup errors may be swallowed and setup failures can leak fixtures. Runner can enumerate unrelated active organizations.
items.fix: Dedicated ephemeral test target, fail-fast target assertion, tracked setup cleanup and surfaced deletion failures; constrain runner fixtures.
items.regression: Inject setup/delete failures and sentinel tenant; no leaks or unintended visits. Production database use was NOT established.

items.title: Migration count equality is not identity or schema parity
items.verification: Parent source-verified; no live migration/schema check
items.problem: The preflight compares counts, allowing equal-count different-content states. CI lacks fresh-install/upgrade migration exercise. Older notes contain contradictory migrator claims.
items.fix: Compare ordered applied hashes/timestamps and snapshot lineage; isolated fresh-install and upgrade tests; one serialized migration owner.
items.regression: Equal-count changed SQL/timestamp, pending migration and valid history fixtures; prove fresh install and upgrade independently.

items.title: Configuration health is not database readiness or proven disaster recovery
items.verification: Parent health/CI source-verified; external provider controls unknown
items.problem: Health always returns ok based on environment presence. Repo does not prove CI-gated deployment promotion or tested DB/Blob restore and compatible rollback.
items.fix: Separate safe bounded readiness from liveness, schema-version signal, post-deploy smoke gate and recovery runbook/restore rehearsal. Do not change plans without permission.
items.regression: Unreachable DB/schema mismatch returns appropriate readiness failure; demonstrate a restore in an isolated target, not production.

items.title: Missing English translations do not fail the i18n gate
items.verification: Parent check returned 47 missing strings with exit 0; source-verified
items.problem: Missing EN keys are reported but excluded from exit condition; additional unwrapped copy bypasses dictionary entirely.
items.fix: Fill missing/wrapped copy and fail on untranslated keys or enforce explicit ratcheted baseline; update stale architecture documentation.
items.regression: Unknown t() key exits nonzero; complete dictionaries pass; EN/HI dashboard/maintenance/navigation/confirmation remain intelligible.
